ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory CDD/EDD under the AML/CFT Act No. 19 of 2017 and VFSC directives; every UBO holding at or above the 25% threshold must be identified and verified; PEPs, their immediate family members, and close associates are subject to enhanced due diligence, source-of-wealth verification, and senior-management approval of the licensed registered agent; mandatory screening against the UN Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC SDN List, UK HMT Sanctions List, EU Consolidated List, Interpol notices, domestic VFSC/FIU advisories, and adverse-media checks; ongoing transaction monitoring and suspicious transaction reporting to the Vanuatu Financial Intelligence Unit.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Vanuatu Financial Services Commission (VFSC) International Company Name Search and Reservation Portal (VFSC Online Registry, vfsc.vu)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: An International Company name must be in Latin script (English or French); all statutory filings with the VFSC are made in English; the proposed name must be distinguishable from all existing names in the VFSC register and must not be misleading or imply any connection with the Government of Vanuatu; the name must end with the word 'Limited', the abbreviation 'Ltd', or another prescribed cognate indicating limited liability.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Vanuatu (where the name suggests government patronage)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant or its licensed registered agent may file a written reconsideration/appeal with the VFSC Registrar within 14 calendar days of the rejection notice, specifying the grounds distinguishing the proposed name from conflicting register entries or attaching the relevant government consent/licence where rejection is due to a sensitive token; the Registrar must issue a written determination within 30 days; a further administrative review or judicial review application may be filed in the Supreme Court of Vanuatu; alternatively, a new name reservation application may be re-submitted after a rejected or expired reservation.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Acceptable in substance—the statutory registered office must be the physical address of the licensed registered agent (CSP) in Vanuatu and cannot be a pure virtual/digital address without a physical presence; the registered agent must be able to receive government notices and service of process and maintain the company's statutory records at that address.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low for an individual standard IC engaged in non-licensed CAD/BIM outsourcing (estimated less than 5% annual probability of an unannounced on-site inspection of the company itself); however, the VFSC and the FIU conduct periodic, no-notice compliance inspections of licensed registered agents and may demand immediate production of UBO and client due diligence records, requiring the agent to retain full client originals.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: International Companies Act No. 10 of 1993, as amended (particularly Sections 4, 12, 13, 15, and 19)
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Vanuatu Financial Services Commission (International Companies Registry)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Memorandum and Articles of Association filed on Form IC-001 (Application for Incorporation of International Company)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No minimum paid-up capital required for an International Company; share capital may be expressed in any authorized currency and no escrow account or capitalization deposit is required
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: That the subscriber(s) to the Memorandum of Association hereby resolve to incorporate an International Company under the International Companies Act No. 10 of 1993, adopt the name approved by the Vanuatu Financial Services Commission, and subscribe to the authorized share capital as set out in the Memorandum, which share capital is deemed fully subscribed by the initial subscriber(s). FURTHER RESOLVED: That the registered office shall be established at the address of the licensed registered agent in Port Vila, Vanuatu, as filed with the Registry, and that such agent shall be authorized to accept service of process on behalf of the Company. RESOLVED FURTHER: That the following persons are appointed as the first directors and officers: [Name(s)], Director; [Name(s)], Company Secretary. The directors are authorized to execute all documents required to register the Company, open bank accounts, and engage the registered agent. This Resolution shall be effective immediately.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Vanuatu Financial Services Commission – International Companies Registry (online portal or authorized agent)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit a name reservation application through the registered agent or directly via VFSC e-platform, specifying the desired company name and confirming it does not contain restricted terms. The Registry conducts a name availability search and issues a name approval notice. The name is reserved for 30 days.
required_dossiers: Identity of applicant or authorized agent
Copy of registered agent license (if applying via agent)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected as undesirable, the applicant may resubmit with alternative name options or appeal in writing to the Registrar for reconsideration within 10 business days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and Notarization of Memorandum and Articles of Association
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Licensed Registered Agent (for notarization) and Vanuatu Financial Services Commission
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Engage a VFSC-licensed registered agent to prepare the Memorandum and Articles of Association in English, including company name, registered office address, authorized share capital, and statement of liability limitation. The incorporators execute the formation documents before a notary or authorized witness. The registered agent verifies the identity of subscribers and attests to due execution.
required_dossiers: Draft Memorandum and Articles of Association
Notarized consent of first director(s) and subscriber(s)
Passport or national ID copies of subscribers and directors
Certificate of good standing for corporate subscribers (if any)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry identifies defective or incomplete clauses, the registered agent may amend the documents and resubmit within 5 business days. Rejected filings are documented with a deficiency notice identifying exact correction required.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission of Incorporation Application and Payment of Fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Vanuatu Financial Services Commission – International Companies Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the signed and notarized Memorandum and Articles of Association together with Form IC-001 and the prescribed registration fee. Payment is made via bank transfer or electronic payment to the VFSC account, and the receipt is retained for reference. The application is filed with the Registrar who conducts a statutory compliance review against the International Companies Act.
required_dossiers: Copy of notarization and subscriber consents
Payment receipt of official filing fee
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registry queries the application, the registered agent receives a deficiency notice and may resubmit within 10 business days. If the Registrar refuses incorporation, the applicant can file an appeal with the Supreme Court of Vanuatu under the International Companies Act.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Certificate of Incorporation and Issuance of Registry ID
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Vanuatu Financial Services Commission – International Companies Registry
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon approval, the Registrar issues a Certificate of Incorporation specifying the company number, date of creation, and legal status. The company becomes a body corporate from the date stated on the certificate. The Registry also issues a Corporate Registry Profile confirming registered agent, registered office, directors, and shareholders.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Any typographical error in the Certificate should be reported to the Registrar within 5 days for administrative correction by an officer rectification request. No court process required for patent clerical errors.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Post-Incorporation Corporate Formalities and Bank Account Opening
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registered Agent; VFSC Compliance; Licensed Commercial Banks in Vanuatu
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After incorporation, convene the first board meeting, adopt the first board resolution, elect directors and officers, and file the notice of director/resignation with the Registry if required. The registered office address is confirmed by the agent. The company secretary is appointed. With the incorporation documents, open a corporate bank account or engage payment rails (Wire Transfer, Wise). The Company must maintain the registered agent and registered office in Vanuatu continuously.
required_dossiers: Registered agent consent and address confirmation
Bank account application forms and banking declaration
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank refuses an account due to legal compliance concerns, the company may apply to another licensed financial institution or request a compliance clarification letter from the VFSC. If a post-incorporation filing deadline is missed, remedies are available under Section 27 of the Act, allowing late filing upon payment of a late filing fee.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Vanuatu Investment Promotion Authority (IPA) – Department of Industry and Department of Labour, where applicable for physical office operations
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: General Business License (issued by the Vanuatu Department of Customs and Inland Revenue for domestic business operations; not applicable for internationally-focused offshore services)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Vanuatu Department of Environmental Protection and Conservation
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No statutory EIA required for office-based CAD/BIM services. If physical office premises generate only domestic wastewater and solid waste, compliance with the Waste Management Act and national drinking water standards applies. No significant air pollutants, VOC, or industrial discharges are expected; any small electrical or electronic waste must be disposed through licensed recyclers under the Waste Management and Pollution Control Regulations.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: The operating office must obtain a fire safety certificate from the Vanuatu Fire Services and Emergency Operations Centre (within the Vanuatu Police Force) confirming adequate fire extinguishers, emergency exits, and smoke detection. A structural load inspection is not required for leases below 50 occupants, but the employer must file a workplace registration with the Department of Labour for the Office and CAD workstation area, and comply with the Health and Safety at Work Act, including ergonomic workstation guidelines, first aid provisions, and evacuation plans.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Ministry of Finance and Economic Management (MFEM); the Department of Customs and Inland Revenue (DCIR), operating as the integrated Vanuatu Revenue and Customs (VRC), administers VAT, customs duties and the prospective income tax regime; the Vanuatu Financial Services Commission (VFSC) is the competent body for incorporation and company registration; filings are effected through the VRC electronic services portal and the VFSC online registry.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: For a Vanuatu International Company (IC): (1) appoint a VFSC-licensed Registered Agent; (2) file the Articles of Association and statutory declarations with the VFSC and pay the fixed registration fee; (3) obtain the Certificate of Incorporation bearing the unique IC company number, which serves as the identification reference for all tax purposes; (4) by operation of section 194 of the International Companies Act [Cap 222], the IC automatically enjoys a 20-year statutory exemption from all Vanuatu taxes, duties, fees and levies, so no separate TIN is procured unless a domestic taxable activity arises; (5) if the IC creates domestic VAT nexus (e.g., local payroll, property, or supplies to Vanuatu residents), file Form VAT-01 with DCIR/VRC to obtain a VAT registration number; (6) for pure offshore CAD/BIM export service delivery, the IC files no customs declaration and no VAT return but must maintain the incorporation certificate, client contracts, invoices, and inward remittance evidence.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: None. Vanuatu has no check-the-box, pass-through, hybrid mismatch or entity classification election. An International Company is classified by statute as a tax-exempt offshore entity for 20 years; an ordinary domestic company cannot elect IC status, and an IC cannot elect to become taxable. Re-domiciliation into or out of the IC regime is available through VFSC administrative filings, not through any tax election. The Income Tax Act No. 27 of 2023 (residency-based personal income tax, deferred implementation) does not alter the IC's statutory exemption.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (VAT) under the Value Added Tax Act [Cap 240], as amended
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: VT 5,000,000 (approximately USD 42,000) of taxable supplies in a rolling 12-month period triggers compulsory VAT registration; voluntary registration is permitted below the threshold; exports of goods and qualifying services to non-residents are zero-rated and excluded from the domestic threshold calculation.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No national e-invoicing, real-time fiscal clearance, digital stamping, or continuous transaction control mandate is in force; paper or PDF invoices issued in vatu are acceptable. Customs import and export declarations are mandatory and processed electronically through the ASYCUDA World single-window system. Offshore CAD/BIM service exports attract no e-invoicing API or fiscal data reporting obligation.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Goods: zero-rated where exported by the supplier within the statutory export timeframe and supported by evidence of physical removal from Vanuatu. Services: zero-rated where supplied to a non-resident recipient who is outside Vanuatu at the time of supply and the service is performed wholly outside Vanuatu or the benefit is enjoyed outside Vanuatu; electronically delivered offshore BIM, structural drafting and engineering CAD services to overseas clients fall squarely within this exported-service zero-rating. The claim requires the IC's exempt status, a written contract with the foreign counterparty, delivery records, and inward remittance evidence.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (ASYCUDA World) with export entry number for physical goods; not applicable to pure digitally delivered CAD/BIM services
Commercial invoice and detailed service contract identifying the non-resident recipient, service description, currency and consideration
Inward remittance certificate or bank credit advice from a Vanuatu-licensed bank evidencing receipt of foreign currency payment
Proof of non-resident status of the overseas client (e.g., tax residence certificate or registry extract) and evidence the service was not performed in Vanuatu
Electronic delivery and project records (transmission logs, BIM model metadata, milestone sign-offs) substantiating that the service was provided and accepted offshore
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DCIR/VRC audits export zero-rating and refund claims strictly; failure to substantiate export within 180 days or the use of fabricated export documentation exposes the taxpayer to full VAT clawback (15%) plus penalty of up to 200% of the tax shortfall, compound monthly interest on unpaid VAT, and criminal fines up to VT 5,000,000 and/or imprisonment up to 7 years for tax fraud. Directors, registered agents and signatories may incur personal liability, and the IC may lose its 20-year statutory exemption and VFSC good-standing status for transacting with Vanuatu residents or breaching the International Companies Act.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Reserve Bank of Vanuatu (RBV), established under the Reserve Bank of Vanuatu Act [CAP 125], exercising exchange-control supervision pursuant to the Exchange Control Act [CAP 69] and delegated Exchange Control Notices issued to authorized dealer banks.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Vanuatu Vatu (VUV) is convertible on the current account without routine RBV pre-approval for trade-in-services payments, including offshore engineering design and CAD/BIM outsourcing fees, provided the underlying contract and invoice are retained by the authorized dealer. Capital account transactions remain administratively controlled, but an International Company (IC) incorporated under the International Companies Act [CAP 222] is treated as a non-resident entity for exchange-control purposes; accordingly, the IC may lawfully hold multi-currency external accounts (USD, AUD, EUR, NZD) and effect capital remittances without mandatory conversion into VUV. Profit repatriation and intercompany settlement face no statutory repatriation tax or withholding, but the RBV requires that all payments be routed through an authorized dealer or licensed external channel so that balance-of-payments statistics are recorded. The genuine practical barrier is bank compliance appetite and correspondent-bank due diligence, not the legal convertibility ceiling.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: For resident exporters, the Exchange Control Act [CAP 69] compels surrender of foreign-currency export proceeds to an authorized dealer within the prescribed timeline (administratively applied as up to 90 days from receipt) and permits the dealer to require conversion to VUV under standard exchange-control notices. A non-resident International Company registered under the IC Act [CAP 222] is excluded from the surrender and conversion mandate; therefore, all CAD/BIM service export receipts may be retained in the original contract currency, provided documentary evidence of the underlying service export is made available to the settling bank. In every instance, proceeds must pass through the banking system via an authorized dealer or an approved external account (not cash or unregulated crypto) to satisfy the RBV's statistical and anti-money-laundering reporting obligations.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_regulations_complement: The RBV's exchange-control delegation encompasses: (i) licensing of authorized dealer banks; (ii) approval thresholds for external borrowing and offshore securities investment; (iii) reporting of large-value wire transfers above VUV 1,000,000 under the AML/CTF framework. The IC's offshore treasury activity below these thresholds, conducted through a licensed bank, requires no standalone RBV authorization, but annual beneficial-ownership updates must be maintained with the Vanuatu Financial Services Commission (VFSC) and the appointed registered agent.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Multi-Currency Account (USD/AUD/EUR) and optional Capital Escrow Sub-Account
Operational USD/EUR/AUD Account with Capital Escrow Tagging

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Bank of South Pacific (Vanuatu) Ltd (successor to Westpac-Vanuatu)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Corporate Operational Account (VUV/USD) and Term Deposit Collateral Account
Domestic VUV Current Account; Non-Resident IC Services Limited

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: LOW-MEDIUM. Vanuatu does not operate a mature e-money institution licensing regime; no RBV-licensed foreign digital EMI can on-board VU resident clients as a principal, and unlicensed offshore EMI accounts create AML/CTF Act No. 44 of 2014 violations for the IC's directors. An offshore IC may practically use third-country EMIs (e.g., UK-FCA, Singapore-MAS, or AUSTRAC-regulated providers) as a secondary collection rail for small-value client invoices, subject to the EMI's own jurisdiction rules, but the mandatory primary treasury and capital-injection rail must be a SWIFT-connected commercial bank account in Vanuatu or an accepted regional hub (e.g., Hong Kong, Singapore, Australia). Structural recommendation: hold the sanctioned bank account at ANZ or BRED as the anchor, and use a licensed EMI only for low-risk receivables under USD 10,000 per transaction, with automatic monthly sweeps back to the anchor account.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical appearance of at least one director or the appointed authorized signatory at the Vanuatu branch is mandatory at ANZ and BRED for initial account opening; a fully remote onboarding without any in-person step is generally refused by RBV-supervised banks. A licensed Vanuatu registered agent (under the VFSC fiduciary regime) may attend the branch with a board resolution granting opening authority, certifying the directors' identity, and producing notarized passport copies and proof-of-address; in limited COVID-era exceptions and for additional (non-signatory) shareholders, a live video interview is accepted as supplementary CDD. NBV and BSP additionally require a local director or resident agent for post-account-operations correspondence. Budget for one physical trip to Port Vila (or a designated ANZ/BRED international representative office arrangement) as the deterministic clearance step.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Tax-exempt International Company lacking economic substance or demonstrable business purpose
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certificate of Incorporation and Certificate of Good Standing issued by the Vanuatu Financial Services Commission (VFSC); registered agent confirmation letter; board resolution approving the account opening; the IC's audited or management accounts; and the executed ISIC 7110 BIM/CAD service master agreement with the offshore client.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Source of funds ambiguity for the initial capital injection (common when the parent holds revenues in China or Hong Kong)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized source-of-funds declaration; 12-month bank statements of the contributing shareholder; corporate chart of the ownership chain; copy of the ultimate beneficial owner's passport and proof of address; and a professional reference letter from a licensed accountant or attorney.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership opacity due to bearer-share history or nominee arrangements
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Completed statutory beneficial-ownership register under the IC Act; executed declaration of trust for any nominee shareholder; certificate of incumbency; certified copies of directors' and shareholders' IDs; and a sworn undertaking to update the register within 30 days of any change.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions-lookalike or origin-of-funds from a higher-risk jurisdiction in the CAD/BIM supplier chain
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Institutional sanctions-screening report (World-Check/Refinitiv) for all counterparties; underlying service contract, purchase orders, and invoices; professional indemnity insurance certificate; and an expected-transaction profile evidencing that outbound payments match genuine subcontractor or software-license disbursements only.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Wire-transfer counterparties classified as high-risk (e.g., client in a jurisdiction subject to FATF enhanced monitoring)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Full contract file with client identity verification; SWIFT MT103 history demonstrating consistent invoice volumes; bank confirmation of no cash or unregulated cryptocurrency involvement; and a legal opinion (when requested) confirming the service is non-regulated design engineering, not export-controlled technology.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Shareholder equity or intercompany loan injections must be wired via SWIFT MT103 from the parent's regulated bank account to the IC's external USD/AUD account at ANZ or BRED. For equity, the bank requires: (i) the IC's board resolution approving the allotment and account credit; (ii) the shareholder subscription agreement; and (iii) book-entry confirmation on the IC's register of members. For intercompany loans, a signed facility agreement with arm's-length interest (no Vanuatu withholding tax applies) and clear repayment schedule is required. The MT103 must state in Field 70/77B a plain-language purpose, e.g., 'Share capital contribution to Vanuatu International Company - BIM/CAD services' for equity, or 'Performance-based intercompany loan for working capital'; Vanuatu has no nationally standardized ISO 20022 purpose-code registry, so authorized dealers typically map the narrative to 'Trade in Services – Computer and Information Services' for BOP reporting. Amounts above VUV 1,000,000 (approx. USD 8,300) trigger automatic AML/CTF reporting; amounts above USD 100,000 will normally require the underlying contract and invoice to be provided to the bank before credit confirmation.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Primary rail: direct SWIFT MT103 full-value transfers from the IC's multi-currency account at ANZ/BRED, with USD cleared via the bank's New York correspondent (typically JPMorgan/HSBC) and AUD via the Sydney network; intra-region supplier payments in Hong Kong or Singapore settle via the bank's Asian correspondent grid. The dominant operating model for the ISIC 7110 outsourcing business is invoice-based payables for subcontract drafting, cloud BIM licensing, and professional indemnity premiums; these are executed as plain MT103 'B2B' payments supported by the supplier's commercial invoice. For large subcontract awards exceeding USD 250,000, a Commercial Letter of Credit is available from ANZ or BRED but is unusual in services; an SBLC issued in favor of the principal client is the more relevant instrument, with the IC's own bank as advising bank. No RBV pre-approval is required for outbound service payments from a non-resident IC external account, but the bank will demand the invoice, the signed service agreement segment, and confirmation that the recipient is not on any sanctions list. Settlement timing is typically T+1 for USD/AUD/EUR; VUV clearing for any residual domestic expenses is executed through the same bank's local clearing system.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Onshore FX Forwards (USD/AUD/EUR vs VUV and major crosses) written by authorized dealers (ANZ, BRED) for genuine commercial exposure up to 12 months; prohibited for speculative positions under Exchange Control Act [CAP 69].

Offshore Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) in VUV executed by the IC's international counterparties (Singapore/Hong Kong desks) when hedging VUV-denominated residual receipts; Vanuatu banks may act as advisers but do not maintain a liquid onshore NDF market.

Cross-Currency Swaps between USD, AUD, and EUR for balance-sheet hedging of multi-currency receivables and contractor payables, permitted upon demonstration of underlying service-trade exposure and recorded by the authorized dealer.

Plain Vanilla FX Options on liquid pairs (USD/AUD, USD/EUR) available on a request-for-quote basis from ANZ/BRED treasury desks for large single exposures above USD 500,000; premium payments are freely remittable as financial-services expenses.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return and Annual Government License Fee under the International Companies Act [Cap 222]
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On or before the anniversary of the date of incorporation; no statutory extension is available
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late fee of VT 5,000 payable for a breach of filing, plus VT 500 per month or part-month of continued default; arrears outstanding beyond 60 days expose the company to administrative deregistration and strike-off from the International Companies Register

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Registered Agent Annual Compliance Declaration (Registered Office, Registered Agent and Solvency Confirmation)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: VFSC through the appointed Vanuatu registered agent
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 14 days after the anniversary of incorporation if requested by VFSC; otherwise the registered agent must maintain a signed compliance declaration in its client file and produce it to VFSC upon supervisory request
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to maintain a valid registered agent and registered office is a continuing offence under the International Companies Act and may lead to VFSC-initiated deregistration without further notice

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Beneficial Ownership Confirmation and Share Register Update Statement
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Vanuatu registered agent acting under the VFSC AML/CFT Rules
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: On the anniversary of incorporation and within 14 days after any transfer of shares or change in beneficial ownership
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-compliance constitutes an AML/CFT supervisory breach; penalties range from formal caution to fines of up to VT 10,000,000 for licensed agents, and continued lapses may result in reporting to VFSC and deregistration of the company

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No statutory audit is compulsory for an International Company holding the standard IC licence. A mandatory independent audit may be required if the company conducts licensed financial or fiduciary activity, holds client money, or is expressly directed by VFSC through a supervisory intervention for non-compliance or material error.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: International Companies Act [Cap 222]; financial records must reflect a true and fair view of the company's transactions. IFRS is acceptable for voluntary audited or compiled financial statements; Vanuatu Local GAAP is not separately codified for International Companies.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Beneficial ownership information is not recorded in any public filing with VFSC. The Vanuatu registered agent must maintain a confidential beneficial ownership register under the VFSC AML/CFT Rules. Directors must provide an annual confirmation of all shareholders with 25% or more ultimate ownership and must notify the registered agent within 14 days of any share transfer or change in UBO. Share transfers are valid only upon entry in the Register of Members.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: US$450–US$1,200 per annum for registered agent fees, registered office, and compliance administration
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: US$0–US$8,000; certified audit not required for a standard IC, voluntary audit fee typically US$4,000–US$8,000, while an annual compilation or bookkeeping review by a professional firm typically costs US$1,500–US$3,000

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: International Companies are fully exempt from Vanuatu corporate income tax, branch profit tax, capital gains tax, stamp duty and all direct taxes. No tax holiday or preferential deduction is required; the only state charges are the annual VFSC registration and licensed agent fees.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: None for corporate income tax (zero-tax regime). The only annual filing is the IC Annual Return (Form 2) submitted to the Vanuatu Financial Services Commission (VFSC) through the licensed registered agent via the VFSC e-portal.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due no later than 30 days after the anniversary of incorporation; not linked to a financial year-end.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: The Form 2 filing contains IC name, registration number, registered office address, registered agent name, directors, shareholders and a declaration that no Vanuatu resident business was transacted. No income, loss, deduction or tax computation boxes are provided because no CIT applies.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident IC shareholder must not enter Vanuatu tax particulars. The registered agent obtains beneficial-owner declarations, files the return and maintains the entity's tax-exempt status.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing penalty: VT 5,000 per month or part thereof, capped at VT 50,000. Continued failure may result in VFSC strike-off and loss of the zero-tax exemption.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Not required in Vanuatu as there is no source-country withholding tax. Vanuatu has no comprehensive DTA network and does not issue Tax Residency Certificates for International Companies. Shareholders seeking foreign tax credits may obtain from the registered agent a Certificate of Incorporation and Certificate of Good Standing; no VFSC tax certification stamp is needed.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory rate: 0% on both interest and royalty payments to non-residents. Without DTAs, treaty-reduced rates are inapplicable; payments leave Vanuatu with no tax leakage.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: No threshold (N/A) — Vanuatu has no transfer pricing legislation and no local file/master file requirement. If the IC belongs to a multinational group, foreign parent-tax rules may nevertheless compel group-level documentation.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Vanuatu's Economic Substance Regulations 2019 apply only to companies carrying on certain mobile activities. A pure offshore CAD/BIM provider with no Vanuatu staff, no Vanuatu office and no management in Vanuatu is outside the ESR scope. If it ever claims domestic service-centre substance in Vanuatu, it must satisfy annual substance reporting: adequate premises, full-time employees and adequate expenditure proportionate to income.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Tax evasion / abuse of zero-tax regime
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Channeling income from real engineering services performed abroad while failing to genuinely manage the entity in a tax-appropriate manner, or deriving revenue from Vanuatu residents using the offshore IC without domestic registration.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the International Companies Act, the company may be fined up to VT 2,000,000; VFSC may strike off the company, revoke the exempt status and render the entity liable to VAT at 12% on any domestic supplies.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly participate may face joint and several civil liability, restitution orders, travel bans during investigation, and imprisonment up to 2 years.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining the IC as a letterbox with no office, no employees, no accounting records, and no demonstrable business activity; failing to file annual returns for consecutive years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Strike-off from the International Companies Register; administrative penalty up to VT 500,000; contracts concluded after strike-off are void and any foreign court may disregard the separate legal personality.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors can be personally liable for debts incurred after strike-off; Supreme Court may issue claw-back orders over dividends and director fees, disqualification for up to 5 years, and travel bans in asset-recovery proceedings.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML/CFT failure and sanctioned payment rails
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Receiving fees through Wise/wire transfers from high-risk or sanctioned sources without implementing CDD/EDD, or concealing beneficial owners from the registered agent and VFSC.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorist Financing Act, a corporate penalty of up to VT 10,000,000; VFSC can freeze bank accounts, suspend the registered agent, and contest any Certificate of Good Standing.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and compliance officers face criminal fines up to VT 5,000,000, imprisonment up to 10 years, confiscation orders under the Proceeds of Crime Act, and travel bans pending trial.
